Anchor.Prefix: the server runs on Node alone.
Anchor.Suffix: : a small router of its own for

Applied.Outcome: Applied: express is dropped and server/app.js is rewritten on node:http (router, JSON body, SSE stream, static files), so an installed copy runs on Node alone and nothing is installed at launch. launch.js and the mod are unchanged; package.json has no dependencies. The Readme section no longer mentions a first-launch install.

Replies.Text: The installed copy has no node_modules, so the server cannot start as the repository stands. Proposal: launch.js runs npm install once when express is missing, which keeps the server as it is and needs npm on the installer's PATH (it comes with Node). Alternative: drop express and write the server on node:http, so an install copy runs with nothing to fetch, at the cost of rewriting the routes and the static file serving. Recommended: the npm install at launch. Agreed?
drop express and write the server on node:http

Anchor.Suffix: , so an installed plugin is keye

Applied.Outcome: Applied: the marketplace is named mchiver; the plugin is keyed claudit@mchiver and the install line is unchanged.

Replies.Text: The marketplace name shows in what the installer sees ("Add marketplace?" names the source, and the plugin is keyed claudit@<marketplace>). Proposal: claudit, since the repository holds this one plugin. Alternative: mchiver, if other plugins of yours should later be installed from one marketplace. Which name?

Applied.Outcome: Applied: .consensus/, .definitions/, .guides/ and CLAUDE.md leave the public repository (removed from the index, ignored), staying on disk untracked; version control of their own is a later plan. They stay in the pushed history, which is not rewritten.

Replies.Text: The .consensus folder (plans, threads, build logs), .definitions, .guides and CLAUDE.md all go into every installed copy. Proposal: keep them in the repository, since it is public already and they are the record of how Claudit was designed. Alternative: move .consensus out of the repository before publishing. Keep them?
i would actualy prefer that they not be in the public repo. they are part of how we make the project and are not part of the project themselves.
